Directions: **Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

There is no reason why you should remain tense when __I was promising to help you.__

options.text: I have promised to help you

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3), i.e. __I have promised to help you__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ffa1a4257a8dc3742a46bf40cbd5271d1530acc0a9b325f76162e3f6b05831a3.png] In the underlined segment, past continuous tense is used and it is incorrect.

__
 
• Past continuous tense should be used to describe an action which was going on when another incident happened__. __Example__: She was singing when her father came back.
 
• But the given sentence talks about an event which has __happened before now but it has some present consequences__. 
 
• Therefore, present perfect tense should be used here.
 
• So, 'was promising' should be replaced with 'have promised'.
 
• Hence, option 3) is the best fit.

questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the correct option:

Switch off the air conditioner ______ you will catch a cold.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1), i.e. '__or__'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ffa1a4257a8dc3742a46bf40cbd5271d1530acc0a9b325f76162e3f6b05831a3.png] There are __two clauses __in the given sentence. Therefore, a conjunction is required here to join these two clauses.

__
 
• 'but' is used to join clauses which are contrasting with each other__. __Example__: She is coming but we can't wait for her. Therefore, option 2) is not the answer.
 
• 'and' is used to join clauses or word which __should be written together__. __Example__: She will buy a book and some flowers for her sister. Hence, option 3) is not the answer.
 
• 'so' means '__therefore__'. __Example__: She is unwell so she will not come.
 
• 'or' means '__otherwise__'. __Example__: You should go now or you will miss the train.
 
• Hence, option 1) is the best fit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/655fefafb1af4f227d2be619fd1b8d204c970cf96a418d5187ec7dfa72e168d0.png] The word which joins __clauses or sentences or words __is called 'conjunction'. 'And','But' yet' are examples of conjunctions.

__
 
• There are three types of conjunctions__:

 __
 
• Coordinating Conjunction
 
• Subordinating Conjunction
 
• Correlative Conjunction
 
 
 
• Coordinating Conjunction__:The conjunction which joins __words, phrases and clauses__ is called 'coordinating conjunction'.
 __
 
• Example__: And, but , yet, so etc. are the examples of coordinating conjunction.
 
 
 
• __Subordinating Conjunction__: Words like because, although, since, till etc. are the examples of subordinating conjunction which joins a __subordinate clause with a main clause__.
 
• __Correlative Conjunction__: The paired words which join phrases, words or clauses are called 'correlative conjunction'.
 __
 
• Example__: Not only....but also, Neither .... nor etc. are the example of 'correlative conjunction'.

questions.solution:

• '**whom**' cannot be chosen because it is used as the object of the verb or a pronoun__. __**Example**__: I don't know the person whom my sister has invited.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ffa1a4257a8dc3742a46bf40cbd5271d1530acc0a9b325f76162e3f6b05831a3.png] The given is a **type 2 conditional sentence**. 

__
 
• In a type 2 conditional sentence, '**simple past tense**' is used with the '**if clause**' and a hypothetical situation__ is mentioned in the **main clause**.

 __
 
• **Example**__:
